qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Cellnex owns physically irreplaceable mobile tower infrastructure with high local permitting barriers, but captive MNO sale-and-leaseback MSAs feature contractual escalator caps (1-3%) that lagged Eurozone inflation. Crucially, multi-year GAAP ROIC is negative to sub-2% due to an inflated ZIRP acquisition asset base and heavy debt burden, completely failing the 12% capital return hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (G3 Moat & Pricing). European tower infrastructure rollup with structurally depressed returns on capital (multi-year GAAP ROIC negative to sub-2%, unlevered ROIC ~3-4%) far below the 12% hurdle. Long-term MSAs contain capped escalators (1-3%) that failed to protect against inflation.
qualitative.evidence: Cellnex pursued an aggressive debt-fueled pan-European tower acquisition spree, accumulating over €17B in net debt and heavy PPA amortization. As a result, reported GAAP net income has been consistently negative (-€297m in 2022, -€297m in 2023, -€28m in 2024), and unlevered ROIC remains mired at 3-4%. Tenant consolidation among European MNOs further restricts pricing power.
